comment: Updated from the partial review. Lone species-C particle, checked against the P-0002 model.py reflected-line predictor with compare_model_r3.py. Earlier: r3/010 (speed 1.0, 12 units, one x=10 wall hit): rms 0.052/0.049, 0 events. Now the edge tests the claim was written for: r1/014 (speed 8.6, 40 units, many bounces): rms_x 0.052, rms_y 0.050, mean residual below 0.002, max |res| 0.149, 0 events. r1/015 (exact corner hit from (8,8) with v (3,3), 20 units): rms 0.048/0.048, mean below 0.004, max |res| 0.175, 0 events. r1/016 (speed 0.22, 100 units): rms 0.050/0.049, mean below 0.001 (no drift), max |res| 0.188, 0 events. All residuals are at tracker noise (about 0.05 per coordinate). Verdict: replicated within the claim's stated domain (lone species C, no drift, specular walls), and the claim also holds at speeds 0.22 to 8.6, durations up to 100 and at a corner hit. Not tested: a lone particle at a wall with a grazing angle below about 0.2 rad, and species other than C (P-0001 covers species A). The claim's predicted_error of 0.01 normalised is consistent with these residuals (2x rms / L = 0.01).
